claim: price_ranges.mid_market: "$80-$250 per location per month (about $10-$25 per monitored unit plus a $29-$150 platform/hub fee), often plus $50-$115 per sensor of installation or configuration"
problem: Unit misstatement on the upper bound of the install band. The $49.99-$69.99 figures from Standard Merchant Services are genuinely per sensor, but the $115 from Kitchen Brains is a one-time configuration fee attached to the TMS subscription, not a per-sensor charge. Presenting the band as "per sensor" overstates it. The same error is repeated in one_line ("often plus $50-$115 per-sensor install").
fix: Rewrite as "plus roughly $50-$70 per sensor of onboarding/installation (Standard Merchant Services $69.99/$59.99/$49.99 per sensor), with separate one-time configuration fees on top (e.g. Kitchen Brains $115 configuration, ChirpDat $495 per zone)". Correct one_line to match.

claim: price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: "$0-$45 per month, or $149-$300 one-time hardware, equivalent to roughly $5-$15 per sensor per month"
problem: The $300 hardware endpoint does not follow from any price in offerings or buyer_reported_costs. Confirmed one-time hardware there tops out at $219.70 (Sensor Easy Starter Kit); TemperatureWise adds $200/sensor and gateways of $100/$250/$450; Kitchen Brains is $529 gateway + $184 sensor (not a self-serve low-cost option).
fix: Change to "$149-$250 one-time hardware" (Temp Stick $149; TemperatureWise $200 sensor / $250 gateway; Sensor Easy $219.70 kit), or delete the $300 endpoint.

problem: The $25 monitored-unit endpoint has no source inside offerings. Highest confirmed recurring per-unit price there is TemperatureWise at $250 per sensor per year, i.e. about $21/month. The only $25-per-sensor figures seen ($25/site/year in the school bid; Crafted Coolers' $25/sensor/month) are either a different unit or appear only in caveats.
fix: Change to "about $10-$21 per monitored unit", or add the specific source for a $25 per-unit month and re-label it as coming from outside the offerings set.

claim: buyer_reported_costs: "Sensitii advertises $79 per location per month including two sensors, with additional sensors at $7/month each" cited to https://sensitii.com/pricing/
problem: The cited page does not contain these numbers. On re-fetch the live pricing page is quote-only ("we quote in writing after seeing your kitchen", "Core is available today", no figures). The $79 + $7 figures only appear in a search-indexed summary of that URL. Source_url therefore does not support the number, even though the finding itself flags it as an older rate.
fix: Either drop the row, or re-label the source as a search-indexed/cached version of the vendor pricing page with a note that the live page no longer shows it, and keep the existing caveat. Do not present it under the live pricing-page URL.

claim: caveats: "TemperatureWise's $250/sensor/year and Sensitii's $79/location were only visible in search-indexed versions of the vendor pages"
problem: Contradicted on the TemperatureWise half. The live page at renyergytech.com/temperaturewise states "$250 per sensor per year, about $21 a month", plus the three restaurant examples ($175 up front/$750 a year; $1,050 up front/$1,000 a year; $2,500 up front/$2,300 a year), and says prices were checked 18 October 2026 against a 1 September 2026 price list. The same caveat sentence also lists TemperatureWise among pages that "rendered prices on fetch", so it contradicts itself. Only the Sensitii half is true.
fix: Delete TemperatureWise from that caveat and state instead that its price list is live and dated 1 Sep 2026 (checked 18 Oct 2026). Optionally add the hardware prices the live page now publishes: $200/sensor, $25 Bluetooth sensor, gateway $100/$250/$450, cellular $125 once + $50/year.

claim: implications_for_consultancy #1: "roughly $99-$199 per location per month ... because that sits below ConnectedFresh's own typical $190-$210/month for a 4-6 unit restaurant"
problem: Internal inconsistency: $199 is not below $190. At 4-6 units the ConnectedFresh equivalent is $190-$210, so the top of the proposed band overlaps rather than sits below it. Inference label is present, but the comparison as written is wrong.
fix: Either narrow the band (e.g. $99-$189) or restate the comparison as "at or below ConnectedFresh's $190-$210/month for 4-6 units, and clearly below it at 7-8 units where ConnectedFresh would price near $230-$250".

claim: implications_for_consultancy #3: "Every serious competitor bundles unlimited users (ThermoWorks Business tiers, Standard Merchant Services 12-month, Sensitii, ConnectedFresh)"
problem: The ConnectedFresh citation does not support it: its cost article says nothing about user counts. The other three are supported (ThermoWorks Business Pro/Business Pro Plus "Unlimited Users"; SMS 12-month "Unlimited Users"; Sensitii "never per seat" / unlimited users).
fix: Replace ConnectedFresh with SmartSense (how-to-buy lists "Unlimited users" among included items), which is verifiable, or drop ConnectedFresh from the list.

claim: implications_for_consultancy #5 and #8: "Sensor Easy 30-day guarantee, Senso/SmartSense style pilots" and "SmartSense, ComplianceMate and SensoScientific all hide prices behind quotes"
problem: Unsupported vendor references. "Senso" appears nowhere else in the brief and has no cited source; SensoScientific is never cited to a URL, only asserted in caveats/data_gaps. "SmartSense style pilots" is also unsourced: the only SmartSense trial language found is nothing at all on how-to-buy (the 45-day trial is Monnit's, not SmartSense's).
fix: Delete the Senso reference and the "SmartSense style pilots" phrase, or cite a page. For the quote-only claim, restrict it to the vendors with cited sources (SmartSense how-to-buy, ComplianceMate/Ladle FAQ) and either cite SensoScientific or remove it.

claim: offerings/Ideal Sciences: "Sensor plus unlimited data logging, 24/7 monitoring and alerts for the life of the sensor"
problem: "For the life of the sensor" is not stated on tempstick.com/common-questions. The page says "no fees or subscriptions", "all accounts are free", "unlimited history" and "continuous monitoring and alert notifications all year round without paying a monthly fee or subscription charge". The lifetime wording is an inference presented as included-feature fact.
fix: Reword to what the page says (no fees or subscriptions, unlimited history, continuous monitoring and alerts) or label the lifetime framing as an inference.

problem: Minor dating error. The cited page (ustechautomations / US Tech Automations comparison) is titled as the 2027 edition, not 2026, although the URL slug says 2026. The prices themselves check out exactly (Year 1 $5,000-$10,500; Year 2+ $1,200-$3,000 per location).
fix: Label the year as "2027 edition, retrieved 2026-11-12" so the reader can judge freshness.

claim: buyer_reported_costs: school-district bid "monitoring at $25 per site per year" and "installation at $450 per address" attributed to SmartSense
problem: The document does contain "$25/site per year" and "$450 installation per address", and now that it has been opened the $175/sensor-with-display and $400/gateway figures are visible in the SmartSense column. But the table flattens on extraction, so the $450/address cell cannot be tied to the SmartSense column with confidence; it may belong to another bidder's column. The brief's own context note ("summary not opened directly") is now outdated.
fix: Keep the figures but add a caution that column-to-price mapping in the bid table could not be confirmed, or limit the quoted numbers to the ones clearly inside the SmartSense column ($175/sensor with display, $400/gateway).
